To confer with others in order to come to terms or reach an agreement.

examples.text:
1963, Martin Luther King, Jr., to the eight fellow clergymen who opposed the civil rights action, "Letter from Birmingham Jail," Why We Can't Wait
"You are quite right in calling for negotiation. Indeed, this is the very purpose of direct action. Nonviolent direct action seeks to create such a crisis and foster such a tension that a community which has constantly refused to negotiate is forced to confront the issue."

glosses: To arrange or settle something by mutual agreement.

examples.text: We negotiated the contract to everyone's satisfaction.
The client and server computers must first negotiate a network protocol to be used.

Hidden behind thickets of acronyms and gorse bushes of detail, a new great game is under way across the globe.[…]The current power play consists of an extraordinary range of countries simultaneously sitting down to negotiate big free trade and investment agreements.

glosses: To succeed in coping with, getting over or navigate a hazard or obstacle.

examples.text: We negotiated the mountain track with difficulty.
Although the car was quite rickety, he could negotiate the curves very well.
Novak Djokovic earlier had negotiated his own tricky passage through the fifth day.

glosses: To transfer to another person with all the rights of the original holder; to pass, as a bill.
To transact business; to carry on trade.

examples.text: Jews, Turks, Armenians,[…]negotiating in this famous Emporium.

glosses: To intrigue; to scheme.

examples.text: Certaine it is, shee was a busie negotiating woman.

glosses: An agreement between parties concerning the sale of property; or a contract by which one party binds themself to transfer the right to some property for a consideration, and the other party binds themself to receive the property and pay the consideration.

examples.text: A contract is a bargain that is legally binding.

glosses: An agreement or stipulation; mutual pledge.

examples.text:
[…]And when your honors mean to solemnize
 The bargain of your faith, I do beseech you,
 Even at that time I may be married too.

glosses: An item purchased for significantly less than the usual, or recommended, price
A gainful transaction; an advantageous purchase.

examples.text: to buy (something) at a bargain
At that price, it’s not just a bargain, it’s a steal.

Thus the red damask curtains which now shut out the fog-laden, drizzling atmosphere of the Marylebone Road, had cost a mere song, and yet they might have been warranted to last another thirty years. A great bargain also had been the excellent Axminster carpet which covered the floor;[…].

glosses: The thing stipulated or purchased.

examples.text: If he say so, may his pernicious soul Rot half a grain a day! He lies to th' heart. She was too fond of her most filthy bargain.

glosses: To make a bargain; to make a deal or contract for the exchange of property or services; to negotiate; to haggle.

examples.text: They had to bargain for a few minutes to get a decent price for the rug.

glosses: To transfer for a consideration; to barter; to trade
To argue for a better deal, especially over prices with a seller.

examples.text: I haggled for a better price because the original price was too high.

examples.text:

glosses: Demander le prix d’une chose, d’un produit, et le plus souvent, en débattre pour obtenir un prix inférieur au prix proposé.

examples.text: M. Marsillat marchande toutes les pouliches du pays sans rien acheter ! ou bien, quand il achète, il fait semblant de se dégoûter bien vite, et il revient pour troquer.

examples.text: Il a manqué cette affaire, à force de marchander.

examples.text: Il n’y a pas à marchander, il faut se décider.

glosses: Accorder sans lésiner.
